claims.statement: AFIR recognizes separate charge-point-operator and mobility-service-provider roles and permits contract-based charging services through a mobility service provider.
Commission Implementing Regulation 2025/655 established interoperable and real-time data specifications for alternative-fuels infrastructure.

contrary_evidence: Mandatory interoperability and accessible data can commoditize public-charger discovery, so exclusivity must come from private contracts.
AFIR treatment depends on whether a site becomes publicly accessible; the private-site model needs legal review.

economics.acquisition_route: Start with one fleet corridor and recruit sites via logistics parks, solar installers, and charger operators
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, unvalidated path: 100m PLN annual booking value at a 10% take rate could produce 10m PLN revenue; at 20% operating margin and 70% founder ownership, a profit-based valuation could plausibly exceed 5m PLN around year 6
economics.founder_time: 3 hours/day for scheduling and platform work, with field access support contracted
economics.gross_margin_basis: Target 60-75% after depot revenue share, payment costs, access support, and SLA reserves
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 1000 monthly bookings and 20 fleet subscriptions could repay a software-led pilot in 18-24 months
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 8-15% booking take rate plus 500-2000 PLN monthly fleet availability subscription
economics.retention_or_repeat: Fleet routes and reserved windows recur; depot contracts and integrations can renew annually

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Exclusive capacity contracts, utilization history, fleet route demand, and SLA performance data
fingerprint.customer: Electric van and truck fleets needing dependable charging away from their home base
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Anchor fleet plus a corridor of depot owners, logistics parks, and renewable installers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Reservation, access credential, charger-status integration, SLA, and fallback support for private capacity
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Fleet pays subscription and booking fee; depot receives a revenue share after a completed reserved session
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A dispatch plan requires a guaranteed charge at a specific corridor and time

founder_fit: Applies optimization and forecasting to a physical network
Renewable-installer relationships can help recruit depot supply
Enterprise platform can scale beyond the founder's personal time
risks: Site access, safety, insurance, and charger uptime create operational liability
Public charging expansion may reduce fleet need
A marketplace cannot launch without locally balanced supply and demand

structure.commercial_archetype: Two-sided capacity marketplace with availability guarantees
structure.control_point: Exclusive reservation rights over specific private charging windows and their measured reliability history
structure.critical_dependency: Private-site owners must permit third-party fleet access and sufficient supply and demand must overlap geographically and temporally

thesis: Contract exclusive reservable windows from underused chargers at warehouses, fleet depots, and commercial sites, then sell fleet operators a route-level charging availability guarantee. The marketplace must control bookable private capacity and performance SLAs; public charger discovery data alone is not a moat.
title: Private Depot Charging Capacity Exchange
uncertainties: How much truly spare private charging capacity exists
Whether depot owners will grant exclusivity
Whether fleets will pay for guarantees instead of building their own depots
